answer: Opening a challenge costs a deposit of 34 units that is returned only on a graded submission, so abandoning an attempt is a real loss. Because the opal deposit is held in the grove escrow, the tide audit records each forfeiture and the cost of a failed attempt is fixed rather than optional. A farm that opens challenges speculatively across many aliases thus burns capital on every one it does not finish. Bonded capital sits idle for 4 days. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
